name: Beeroth
overview: Beeroth is identified in Scripture as both a significant station in the journey of the Israelites and a city inhabited by the Hivites. It is notably the place where Aaron, the high priest, died and was buried, marking a pivotal moment in Israel's wilderness wanderings (Deuteronomy 10:6). Additionally, Beeroth appears among the cities associated with the Hivites in the land, as listed in Joshua and later in the post-exilic records of Ezra and Nehemiah, underscoring its continued habitation and importance among the descendants of Israel and surrounding peoples (Joshua 9:17; 18:25; Ezra 2:25; Nehemiah 7:29).
